title: Balanced finite-tower association and quotient-generator normalization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites put $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}S_{W,n}$, $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$, with specified projections $\pi_{W,n}$ and quotient transitions $q_{n+1,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. All finite levels are restricted along these projections. Write $c_g:g^{-1}R_T\to R_{T'}$ for the projection-induced ring map and $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}R_{T'}$ for ordinary module pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Use unbounded cochain complexes and their derived localizations $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. A good complex means K-flat with flat terms [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]. Set $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with transition $(t,1)$ and augmentation $\epsilon_{W,n}:Q_{W,n}\to S_{W,n}[0]$ equal to $\pi_{W,n}$ in degree zero and zero in degree minus one [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers].

For any $R_T$-complex $P$ write $F(P)_n=P\otimes S_{T,n}$ and $B_g^0(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*F(P)_n$, with the actual quotient transitions [def-a1-integral-finite-pullback-tower, def-pur-integral-finite-pullback]. Let $c_{g,n}:g^{-1}S_{T,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{T',n}$ be the constant-coefficient structural map [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]; it satisfies $\pi_{T',n}c_g=c_{g,n}g^{-1}\pi_{T,n}$.

There are $R_{T'}$-linear natural isomorphisms of strict towers of cochain complexes
$$\lambda_P:(GP\otimes S_{T',n})_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g^0(P),\qquad C_P:(G(F(P)_n))_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g^0(P).$$
Here $\lambda_{P,n}$ identifies both sides with $g^{-1}P\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}S_{T',n}$. The first identification sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes\pi_{T',n}(b)a$, with inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$; the identification from $g_n^*F(P)_n$ sends $(x\otimes z)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes c_{g,n}(z)a$, with inverse inserting $1$ in the $g^{-1}S_{T,n}$ factor. The map $C_{P,n}$ sends a pulled quotient-unit generator $b\otimes g^{-1}(x\otimes1)$ to the finite-pullback generator $g^{-1}(x\otimes1)\otimes\pi_{T',n}(b)$. These formulas define inverse balanced maps of sheaf tensor complexes, commute with restrictions and differentials, are natural for every chain map, and commute with every quotient transition.

For $H(P)_n=P\otimes Q_{T,n}$, $a_P=(1_P\otimes\epsilon_{T,n})_n$, and the ordinary tensor/unitor comparison $\theta_P:GH(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}(GP\otimes Q_{T',n})_n$ (on the two Koszul generators $(x\otimes e_i)\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes b)\otimes e'_i$), there is equality of strict chain maps
$$\lambda_P\circ a_{GP}\circ\theta_P=C_P\circ G(a_P).$$
On the degree-zero Koszul generator both maps use the quotient projection, and on the degree-minus-one generator both are zero. For good $P$, this equality identifies the finite evaluations of the localized zigzag with the prescribed K-flat representative maps and pure-tensor generators of [def-a1-integral-completed-pullback-interfaces]. It retains the specified projections and adjunction-unit generators, rather than permitting an arbitrary automorphism of a finite evaluation. No invertibility assumption is made on $c_g$.
